_: The province node: what nearly everyone in Black Marsh in 4E 201 shares, whatever their region, people or faction. The regions, peoples and factions below it are lanes 2.5a1b and 2.5a2. Every trait cites a lore dossier or says inferred.

norms.text: A place is spoken of as its own country; locals never call the whole marsh one nation.
People live on what the marsh gives: fishing, foraging and small plots, never plantations.
Goods move by raft and river; a raft is trusted over any Imperial road.
The Hist is treated as a fact of life, mentioned in passing like weather or tide.

taboos.text: Calling an Argonian lukiul to their face; it is the nativists' slur for the assimilated.
Praising Umbriel or the men who summoned it.

values.text: Endurance: the marsh has been emptied three times and people stayed.
Local knowledge of water, root and season over any written law.
Freedom from bondage, held hard because the slave trade was the one foreign venture that paid.

contempts.text: Outsiders who come to drain, plant or pave the marsh and leave it worse.
Slavers and anyone still trading in people.

place.text: Home is this stretch of water, not the province; other parts of the marsh are nearly foreign.

work.text: Work is what keeps you fed this season; honest work keeps you poor here.

people.text: Strangers are watched until they show what they want.

faction.text: The Wardens' writ is real at the ports and the border and thin everywhere else.

hist.text: The Hist is older than every race and is not discussed lightly with outsiders.

empire.text: The Empire built roads that rotted the cargo and is gone; few miss it.

trade.text: Saltrice, timber, herbs and hides leave by water; the river is the market.

danger.text: The interior kills: predators, poison, rot and the flu that took whole peoples.

rumour.text: Talk runs on old burns and plagues returning and on what the Wardens hide.

directions.text: Ways are given by water, landmarks and days by raft, not by miles or road names.

addressTerms.text: Outsiders are called by their homeland, rarely by name.

neverSaid.text: Who among the neighbours took the An-Xileel's side in 4E 48.
That a family was once owned, or once owned others.

grievances.text: The Wardens take customs at the ports and give nothing back upriver.
The Wardens never answered for Gideon and Lilmoth.

rumours.text: A fisher saw a light under the bog, like the Great Burn starting again.
